$comment: Probe inputs for the live eval, as DATA — adding a chain here is a config edit, never a code change.
Only the FREE (keyless) capability surface is covered: chain.tvl, protocol.tvl, token.price/metadata,
pairs.active, wallet.balances.native. Nansen-backed tools (entity.labels, smart-money.flows, token.risk)
are excluded on purpose — they spend credits.
A field left absent means 'no probe curated' → that case is reported as `no-probe`, never as a failure.
That distinction matters: an eval that scores its own missing test data as a provider defect is lying.
wallet: the EVM zero address is used deliberately as a universal probe. It is valid on every EVM chain,
needs no per-chain curation, and cannot rot. The check asserts a well-formed balance with the right
symbol/decimals — NOT balance > 0 — because zero is a legitimate answer and asserting otherwise would
make the eval fail on a correct response.
token: a curated contract per chain. An earlier design discovered the address live from pairs.active
instead; the real payload settled it — active_pairs returns baseTokenSymbol and never a contract address,
so that chain does not exist. Cross-provider agreement is checked a different way (see checks.mjs
crossChecks): registry-vs-provider, chain echo, and registry nativeSymbol vs what the RPC reports.
Slugs and addresses here are VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE PROVIDERS, not recalled: a wrong one shows up
as a provider error and would blame the server for a defect in the test data.
referenceSources (TASK-009): a source the ENGINE does not use, fetched directly by the eval to check an
answer against something with no shared cause. Adding one is a config edit here — run.mjs reads url/parse
generically. Rules: https only; the host lives in this reviewed file, never computed at run time; and a
reference that fails to answer yields `no-probe`, never a provider failure, because it is OUR test
apparatus and not the vendor under test.

btcTipHeight.why: Independent of blockchain-info in vendor, infrastructure and funding. It is the only value in the BTC supply answer a second source can genuinely contradict: re-deriving emission from the halving schedule agrees with blockchain.info by construction, because the vendor computes it the same way. mempool.space is deliberately NOT an engine adapter — a source we answer from cannot be the check on that answer.
btcTipHeight.verifiedNote: HTTP 200, content-type text/plain, body '960103'; 8 rapid sequential probes all 200, no RateLimit-* header of any kind

supplyVsConsensus.why: The delta is counted in BLOCKS OF SUBSIDY, never in percent: one block is 0.000016% of supply, so an off-by-one and a full day of staleness (144 blocks, 0.0023%) both round to zero on any percentage scale a human would pick. 6 blocks is about an hour. MEASURED skew across three samples on 2026-07-29 was -2..0 blocks — blockchain.info's /stats is an aggregate with its own refresh cadence, and a block can be found between the two calls; the tool's 600s TTL can add one more. The BOUND itself is DEFENSIVE, not measured, and must not be cited as a vendor ceiling — it lives here as data so it can be retuned without a release.

ethereum.why: reference EVM: the only profile with every free capability at once

solana.why: the only non-EVM family with wallet balances — a different adapter (rpc-solana)
solana.walletNote: System Program — always exists, balance may be 0

polygon.why: non-ETH native symbol (POL) — catches symbol/decimals assumptions

berachain.why: serves pairs.active/pool.info WITHOUT the Nansen capabilities — a profile ethereum/solana hide

gnosis.why: wallet balances but no pairs.active and no paid capabilities — the plain long-tail EVM profile

tron.why: non-EVM, non-SVM: token+tvl only, NO wallet balances — the case that must report `unsupported`
tron.tokenNote: USDT TRC20 — non-EVM address format, which is the point of probing it

bitcoin.why: minimal non-EVM profile; no token contracts at all
bitcoin.protocolNote: verified live 2026-07-27; the slug is NOT 'babylon'

zcash.why: this project's privacy focus; the narrowest profile in the registry — chain.tvl + protocol.tvl only
